scenes.visual: Title card: HELICES, SHEETS AND THE RULE-BREAKERS.

scenes.tts: The map has islands. Why do they become helices and sheets?
scenes.visual: The Ramachandran plot with its islands; arrows point from the islands to blank boxes labelled ?. The question appears on screen.
scenes.narration: The map has islands. Why do they become helices and sheets?

scenes.tts: Each island is the geometry of a regular shape. That shape lets the backbone hydrogen bond to itself.
scenes.visual: The helix island morphs into a schematic coil; dashed lines appear inside it, labelled hydrogen bonds.
scenes.narration: Each island is the geometry of a regular shape. That shape lets the backbone hydrogen bond to itself.

scenes.tts: The bonds run between backbone C O groups and N H groups. Shapes built this way are called secondary structure.
scenes.caption: The bonds run between backbone C=O groups and N–H groups. Shapes built this way are called secondary structure.
scenes.visual: Close-up of one dashed line between a C=O and an N–H on the backbone. Label: secondary structure.
scenes.narration: The bonds run between backbone C=O groups and N–H groups. Shapes built this way are called secondary structure.

scenes.tts: Secondary structure is local. It describes a stretch of chain, not the whole protein.
scenes.visual: A long chain with one stretch highlighted. Label: local.
scenes.narration: Secondary structure is local. It describes a stretch of chain, not the whole protein.

scenes.tts: First, the alpha helix. It is a right-handed coil.
scenes.visual: A schematic coil builds, turning to the right. Label: α helix, right-handed.
scenes.narration: First, the alpha helix. It is a right-handed coil.

scenes.tts: It has a little over three and a half residues per turn.
scenes.caption: It has 3.6 residues per turn.
scenes.visual: Dots mark residues around one turn; a counter reads 3.6 residues per turn.
scenes.narration: It has 3.6 residues per turn.

scenes.tts: Inside the helix, each C O group bonds to the N H group four residues ahead.
scenes.caption: Inside the helix, each C=O group bonds to the N–H group four residues ahead.
scenes.visual: Dashed lines light up one by one, each from residue i to residue i+4.
scenes.narration: Inside the helix, each C=O group bonds to the N–H group four residues ahead.

scenes.tts: In the first turn, the N H groups have no partner four residues back. The side chains stick outward.
scenes.visual: The first turn of the coil shows its N–H groups in grey with no dashed line. Short stubs bristle outward from the coil.
scenes.narration: In the first turn, the N–H groups have no partner four residues back. The side chains stick outward.
scenes.caption: In the first turn, the N–H groups have no partner four residues back. The side chains stick outward.

scenes.tts: In a helix, the partners are near each other in the sequence.
scenes.visual: A sequence strip below the coil; brackets join residues four apart. Label: near in sequence.
scenes.narration: In a helix, the partners are near each other in the sequence.

scenes.tts: Second, the beta sheet. Its strands are stretched nearly flat.
scenes.visual: Two flat zigzag arrows appear side by side. Label: β strands.
scenes.narration: Second, the beta sheet. Its strands are stretched nearly flat.

scenes.tts: Side chains alternate, above and below the sheet.
scenes.visual: Stubs on each strand point up, down, up, down.
scenes.narration: Side chains alternate, above and below the sheet.

scenes.tts: Each strand bonds to its neighbouring strands. They can run in the same direction, or in opposite directions.
scenes.visual: Dashed lines zip the strands together. The arrows first point the same way, then one flips. Labels: parallel; antiparallel.
scenes.narration: Each strand bonds to its neighbouring strands. They can run in the same direction, or in opposite directions.

scenes.tts: Those strands can lie far apart in the sequence.
scenes.visual: The sequence strip below: the two strands are colored segments far apart, joined by a long arc. Label: far apart in sequence.
scenes.narration: Those strands can lie far apart in the sequence.

scenes.tts: Now meet a rule-breaker, proline. Its side chain loops back and bonds to its own backbone nitrogen.
scenes.visual: A schematic proline: the side chain curls back and joins the backbone N, closing a ring.
scenes.narration: Now meet a rule-breaker, proline. Its side chain loops back and bonds to its own backbone nitrogen.

scenes.tts: That makes a ring. So proline has no N H group to donate, and its ring is bulky.
scenes.caption: That makes a ring. So proline has no N–H group to donate, and its ring is bulky.
scenes.visual: The N of proline is circled with no H attached. The ring is shaded, labelled bulky.
scenes.narration: That makes a ring. So proline has no N–H group to donate, and its ring is bulky.

scenes.tts: Here is the test. Where in a helix could a proline sit without breaking it?
scenes.visual: A helix with a proline icon hovering above it. On-screen question: where can proline sit?
scenes.narration: Here is the test. Where in a helix could a proline sit without breaking it?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: In the first turn. There, the N H groups have no partners anyway. Losing one costs nothing.
scenes.caption: In the first turn. There, the N–H groups have no partners anyway. Losing one costs nothing.
scenes.visual: The proline drops into the first turn; the helix stays intact. Label: first turn: no partners four back anyway.
scenes.narration: In the first turn. There, the N–H groups have no partners anyway. Losing one costs nothing.

scenes.tts: In the middle, proline breaks the helix. It cannot donate its hydrogen bond.
scenes.visual: A second proline drops into the middle; one dashed line vanishes and the coil kinks.
scenes.narration: In the middle, proline breaks the helix. It cannot donate its hydrogen bond.

scenes.tts: And its ring bumps into the backbone of the turn before it.
scenes.visual: The ring flashes red where it touches the turn above it.
scenes.narration: And its ring bumps into the backbone of the turn before it.

scenes.tts: Its fixed angle is not the problem. That angle is a helical one.
scenes.visual: A small Ramachandran inset: proline's φ marker sits near −65°, inside the helix island.
scenes.narration: Its fixed angle is not the problem. That angle is a helical one.

scenes.tts: The same ring builds something else, collagen. It pre-shapes each strand into an extended helix.
scenes.visual: Three long, loosely coiled strands appear. Label: collagen.
scenes.narration: The same ring builds something else, collagen. It pre-shapes each strand into an extended helix.

scenes.tts: Collagen repeats a pattern, glycine, then two other residues. Those are often proline and hydroxyproline.
scenes.caption: Collagen repeats a pattern: Gly-X-Y. X and Y are often proline and hydroxyproline.
scenes.visual: A repeating sequence strip: Gly-X-Y, Gly-X-Y. X and Y tagged often Pro and Hyp.
scenes.narration: Collagen repeats a pattern: Gly-X-Y. X and Y are often proline and hydroxyproline.

scenes.tts: Three chains wind together into a triple helix. Every third residue sits at the crowded center.
scenes.visual: The three strands twist together. End-on view: every third residue points into the crowded center.
scenes.narration: Three chains wind together into a triple helix. Every third residue sits at the crowded center.

scenes.tts: Only glycine is small enough to fit there.
scenes.visual: The center slot shows a single small H. Label: glycine.
scenes.narration: Only glycine is small enough to fit there.

scenes.tts: Put a larger residue in place of that glycine, in type one collagen. That is a common cause of brittle bone disease.
scenes.caption: Put a larger residue in place of that glycine, in type I collagen. That is a common cause of osteogenesis imperfecta, brittle-bone disease.
scenes.visual: A bulky residue jams the center slot; the strands bulge apart. Label: osteogenesis imperfecta (brittle-bone disease).
scenes.narration: Put a larger residue in place of that glycine, in type I collagen. That is a common cause of osteogenesis imperfecta, brittle-bone disease.

scenes.tts: What kills one structure builds another. One residue, again, decides the shape.
scenes.visual: Side by side: a helix broken by proline; collagen built with proline.
scenes.narration: What kills one structure builds another. One residue, again, decides the shape.

scenes.tts: Geometry allows these local shapes. But it does not choose which ones a protein makes.
scenes.visual: Helices and sheets float apart, unconnected. A question mark: what chooses?
scenes.narration: Geometry allows these local shapes. But it does not choose which ones a protein makes.

scenes.tts: Helices and sheets are the backbone bonding to itself.
scenes.visual: End card. LINE: Helices and sheets are the backbone hydrogen-bonding to itself, in shapes the map allows.
scenes.narration: Helices and sheets are the backbone bonding to itself.
